title: Modern Tech vs Sustainable Green
lede: Two restrained pages, both white, both one accent. They disagree about whether restraint means precision or absence.
verdict: Modern Tech expresses care through technique — a 56px grid fading out behind the hero, mono numerals, an 8px button radius and a 1px shadow. Sustainable Green expresses care by removing all of it: zero box-shadows on the page, system fonts, and 1px rules doing the work borders normally do.
brief: Modern Tech is engineered. The hero sits on a two-axis grid of 1px lines at 56px spacing, masked to fade to nothing by 78% of the way down, so it reads as texture rather than graph paper. Numbers and labels are Roboto Mono, which makes digits align across rows — the detail that makes a product page feel built rather than styled.

Sustainable Green is subtractive. There is not a single box-shadow in the stylesheet. Sections are separated by 1px #dfe3e0 rules, service items are marked with a 2px left border in #1f7a4d instead of a card, and the only font family is the system stack. It is also the fastest page in the gallery, because there is nothing to download beyond one CSS file.

whenA: The page sells something technical and the precision is part of the pitch
There is real data — numbers, figures, statuses — that benefits from mono alignment
You want a designed feel without colour, imagery or ornament
whenB: Page weight and honesty are part of the brand: no webfont, no shadow, nothing decorative
The content is long and mostly text, so rules and whitespace are enough
The organisation is a public body, a co-op or a climate brand where restraint is expected
promptDelta: The deciding clause is whether shadows exist. Say "one accent, system fonts, zero box-shadows, 1px rules between sections" and you get the green page. Say "a faint 56px grid behind the hero that fades out, mono numerals for all figures, 8px button radius with a 1px shadow" and you get the tech page. A model asked for "clean minimal white with a green accent" will produce neither: it will add a webfont, a soft shadow, and land on a generic SaaS look.
